transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 10:00 AM PST / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dina Morales (Redwood SE), Lina Zhao (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Lumina CTO), Marco Li (Lumina Platform), Evan Brooks (Lumina Security), Priya Nair (Lumina SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Discussed POC scope to integrate Redwood SDK using OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function/tool calling. Covered success criteria and benchmark plan.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Samir, AE at Redwood. we'll run through what Lumina needs, scope a pilot, and put concrete success metrics.
00:21 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Thanks. we want to make sure the POC proves two things: one, the models can reliably extract structured fields from detection alerts; two, we can call internal enrichment tools securely during generation flows.
00:45 Speaker 3 (Dina): great — from the tech side we'll propose using our OpenAI-compatible endpoints so you don't have to rewrite existing clients. there are also SDK helpers for function calling and structured output validation.
01:12 Speaker 4 (Marco): when you say OpenAI-compatible, does that include the same response streaming and function calling semantics? we have microservices that expect the same JSON payloads.
01:33 Speaker 2 (Dina): yes, function calling semantics are supported but there are some differences in field names in earlier builds — sorry, the auto-transcripts call it "func call name" vs "tool" naming, but runtime maps them. we'll share the compatibility matrix.
01:57 Speaker 5 (Evan): security concerns: we need VPC-native connections, customer-managed KMS for any keying, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. SOC2 compliance is a must.
02:15 Speaker 1 (Samir): absolutely — Redwood Private can run in your VPC or we can provide a private control plane. we have KMS integrations and detailed audit logs. Samir: i'll send the SOC2 and network diagram after this call.
02:41 Speaker 3 (Lina): quick note on latency: for your synchronous enrichment flows, what's your p95 target?
03:00 Speaker 4 (Marco): ideally under 500ms for 512-token prompts. Some enrichment calls can be async, but critical paths need low tail latency.
03:18 Speaker 3 (Dina): good to note — Redwood can operate in two modes: low-latency optimized (smaller batches, reserved capacity) or cost-optimized (larger batching, quantized models). For the POC we can configure reserved capacity to hit p95 SLOs.
03:47 Speaker 2 (Aisha): success criteria — put here what we'll evaluate: structured extraction accuracy above 95% on our labeled set, p95 latency under 600ms for synchronous flows, end-to-end cost below threshold (we'll give a target per 1k tokens), and secure connectivity with KMS + audit logs.
04:20 Speaker 1 (Samir): capturing that. on the cost we usually present token-based estimates plus reserved capacity options; we'll run a short benchmark to translate your traffic into cost per month.
04:38 Speaker 6 (Priya): about deployment — we prefer Private VPC but might start with Dedicated hosted capacity to iterate faster. timeline depends on security review.
04:55 Speaker 3 (Dina): recommended POC plan: 1) baseline benchmark with OpenAI-compatible endpoint using your prompt set, 2) enable function/tool calling to hit enrichment endpoints, 3) validate structured JSON outputs against your schema, 4) run 48h durability test and collect metrics.
05:25 Speaker 4 (Marco): for the benchmark inputs, we'll share 500 representative prompts and a 48h traffic slice.
05:40 Speaker 1 (Samir): good. for tooling, we have SDKs in Python, Node, and a thin Java client. Which language does your platform use?
05:55 Speaker 4 (Marco): primarily Go and Python for orchestration.
06:08 Speaker 3 (Dina): Python SDK covers function calling helpers and structured output validators; for Go you'll use the OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints, or we can share a sample Go wrapper.
06:27 Speaker 2 (Aisha): how does the function calling map to our internal enrichment services? we want to call an internal REST service to fetch threat intel during generation.
06:44 Speaker 3 (Dina): function calling can trigger a webhook to your service or your sidecar; we support synchronous and asynchronous patterns. note on security: you can restrict keys to specific routes and use mTLS for internal calls.
07:05 Speaker 5 (Evan): any data retention by Redwood in hosted mode? we need ephemeral-only logs for some workloads.
07:18 Speaker 1 (Samir): hosted default retains request/response for 30 days for debugging, but Private deployment and Dedicated reserved capacity can be configured to not store payloads. we'll include retention controls.
07:36 Speaker 6 (Priya): on the structured output: we need strict JSON schema validation and a way to detect hallucinations — do you support automatic validators and fallback to re-run with different temperature?
07:58 Speaker 3 (Dina): yes, SDK includes output validators. we also have an automatic regression check: if the schema fails, you can configure a fallback to a deterministic decoding setting or to a smaller model. additionally, our Optimize tooling will recommend quantization/configs to balance cost vs accuracy.
08:25 Speaker 4 (Marco): benchmarks — what's realistic for us to measure? throughput, p50/p95 latency, token cost, and accuracy on labeled set?
08:40 Speaker 3 (Dina): that's right. we'll run three scenarios: 1) sync enrichment (single-turn, 512 tokens), 2) multi-tool flow (model calls tool then re-runs), 3) batched inference for offline processing. we'll report CPU/GPU utilization too.
09:05 Speaker 2 (Aisha): timeline — we want a demo by end of next week and a 2-week POC after that if possible. Security review will probably take 3 weeks.
09:22 Speaker 1 (Samir): propose: run quick internal bench (Redwood) with your sample prompts in 48h, share results on 11/10, then run a 2-week tenant-scoped POC in your environment week of 11/17 if security sign-off done.
09:45 Speaker 6 (Priya): we will need an offline credentials exchange and a network allowlist.
10:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): noted. we'll provide an allowlist template.
10:12 Speaker 5 (Evan): small nit: how are function call schemas versioned? as our enrichment evolves we need backward compatibility.
10:28 Speaker 3 (Dina): functions are versioned per route; we recommend semantic versioning and Redwood supports canary rollouts so you can test new tool schemas.
10:45 Speaker 4 (Marco): any gotchas with KV cache or session cache when doing multi-turn tool calling?
11:00 Speaker 3 (Dina): relevant — KV cache is per-session and optimized for latency, but if you do stateful enrichment across many small requests we'll configure TTLs and cache eviction. some model variants interact differently with cached keys — we'll call that out in the benchmark notes.
11:22 Speaker 2 (Aisha): one more: instrumentation — we'll want traces with token-level timing. can you forward trace spans to our tracing system?
11:34 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes, we have tracing hooks and can forward OTLP to your collector; we'll confirm retention windows.
11:48 Speaker 6 (Priya): for the demo, can you show both SDK flow (Python) and raw OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests?
12:02 Speaker 3 (Dina): yes, we'll demo both. show how function calling works with your enrichment service mocked.
12:20 Speaker 4 (Marco): regarding cost: if we run reserved capacity, what's min commitment and how do you measure utilization?
12:35 Speaker 1 (Samir): typical reserved tiers start monthly with X GPU-equivalent units; we'll send detailed pricing — there's usually a baseline commit + overage pricing.
12:50 Speaker 5 (Evan): compliance — do you support customer-managed keys only in Private? or can Dedicated be shipped with bring-your-own-key?
13:10 Speaker 3 (Dina): BYOK is available for Private and for Dedicated through an add-on in many cases; we'll confirm for your account.
13:28 Speaker 2 (Aisha): ok, recap and next steps?
13:35 Speaker 1 (Samir): recap: 1) Samir shares SOC2, network diagram, pricing sheet; 2) Marco provides prompt set and traffic slice; 3) Dina runs benchmark and shares metrics; 4) schedule demo next week and plan 2-week POC after security sign-off.
13:56 Speaker 4 (Marco): we'll get the data by Friday.
14:05 Speaker 6 (Priya): can we have a short tech deep-dive with your infra team to validate VPC peering?
14:18 Speaker 3 (Dina): yes, Lina and I will join that.
14:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the docs and calendar invites.

Action recap (auto): Samir to send security docs and pricing; Dina to run benchmarks; Marco to provide sample prompts and traffic; schedule demo and infra deep-dive.

End of transcript.
